Running Inkscape command (e.g. to export a PNG) from terminal or even from standalone Python script that imports `inkscape()` function from `inkex.command` module, while another windowed Inkscape instance is active, gives no crash.


#### Steps to reproduce:

Easiest way to reproduce the crash is to save a file in `.xcf` format. I have to warn about another crash that happens if a 'save-as' extension fails to save a file, this crash is easily fixable (see diff below).

- Open Inkscape
- Draw a rectangle
- Go to 'File -> Save As...' and select `GIMP XCF maintaining layers (*.xcf)` as a file type
- Optionally choose a folder and a filename
- Click 'Save' (GIMP XCF dialog appears)
- Click 'OK' in the dialog
- (Inkscape hangs for a moment)
- (First crash of the child Inkscape instance occurs here)
- (Message window with the Python traceback appears, reporting about `ProgramRunError`)

First crash is the reason of this issue, so I'm describing it.

Inkscape called Python (as extension) which called another GUI-less instance of Inkscape as a subprocess. This Inkscape instance crashed (SIGABRT) due to some error in

#### What should have happened?

Child Inkscape instances should not crash and, as a consequence, extensions should not fail.

Issue:
Ungrouping Can Produce Invalid Clip Paths
<!--
    See our full bug reporting guidelines at https://inkscape.org/contribute/report-bugs/
    Writing a good bug report will ensure we'll be able to help efficiently. 🙂
-->

#### Summary:
<!-- Summarize the issue/suggestion concisely: -->

If Ungroup is performed on a group with a clip path applied to it that contains a single shape, the resulting SVG has a group attribute \<g\> inside the \<clipPath\>. As per the SVG spec, \<g\> is not a valid child of \<clipPath\>, and while Inkscape is able to continue rendering the clipped shape correctly, if the SVG is exported, other apps (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Office) are totally unable to render the clipped shape. Manually deleting the group object from the clip path in the XML so that the path itself is the topmost child results in other apps being able to render it again.

#### Steps to reproduce:
<!-- Describe what you did (step-by-step) so we can reproduce: -->

- Open Inkscape
- Create a group that has a clip path applied to it and that contains a single shape
  - Insert two shapes and group them
  - Insert a third shape and apply it as a clip onto the group
  - Select one of the group member shapes and delete it
- Perform an Ungroup on what remains
- Export the SVG

#### What happened?

If you open the result in a browser, you observe that nothing renders. Viewing the XML confirms that the \<clipPath\> attribute has a \<g\> inside, which is invalid.

#### What should have happened?

The resulting SVG should have a valid XML structure that other apps can interpret and render. The group is not needed within the clip path, and manually removing it restores the expected behavior.

#### Summary:
Normally the stroke of the text will not overlap other text in the same tspan. Export to pdf with text to paths enabled will not preserve this since each letter is separated.

#### Steps to reproduce:

- open Inkscape
- Create some text (e.g. "Friend")
- Give the text negative spacing so that they overlap a bit
- Set a stroke
- Duplicate and Convert the duplicate text to path

#### What happened?
- Since each letter is a separate path, they will overlap each other

#### What should have happened?
- Text that are part of the same text chunk should be combined together.

```shell

inkscape --export-area-page --convert-dpi-method=scale-document -o cli-convert-dpi-method-scale-document.png shapes_pre_0.92.svg 
```

The exported PNGs have unscaled 400 x 300 px sizes.

The exported PNGs should be scaled to 427 x 320 px,

Issue:
inkscape's "internal import" of PDF doesn't render Okular's annotations
#### Summary:
<!-- Summarize the issue/suggestion concisely: -->

If you annotate a PDF using the Okular image viewer then open it in Inkscape using its "Internal import" library, although the preview in the PDF import's Page settings dialog shows all the annotations, none of the annotations are in the resulting drawing.

#### Steps to reproduce:
- open the attached PDF in Inkscape. (I made it by opening a PDF in Okular, annotating with each tool, then File > Save)
- in Inkscape's Page settings dialog, choose "Internal import", not "Poppler/Cairo import"
- click OK

#### What happened?
Although the Page settings dialog previews the PDF showing the annotations, none are visible in Inkscape.

#### What should have happened?
Ideally Inkscape's "Internal import" PDF library would import Okular's annotations along with the PDF.

It would be better if the preview in Inkscape's dialog matched the appearance in Inkscape, i.e. don't show the PDF's annotations if they won't be visible in Inkscape.

Sample attachments:
- [okular_annotations.pdf](/uploads/b7329119df3e8ffb67d06e685183de66/okular_annotations.pdf)
- Here's Inkscape's PDF Page settings dialog ![okular_annotations_inkscape_PDF_dialog](/uploads/7bbe1529a22206afc5b5f287265b9446/okular_annotations_inkscape_PDF_dialog.png)

#### Version Info:

```
- Inkscape Version: 1.0.2 (e86c870879, 2021-01-15), Flatpak version
- Operating System: Fedora
- Operating System version: 33 KDE Spin
```

#### Other notes
If I import using "Poppler/Cairo import" library, the annotations appear in Inkscape. (The exception is Okular's Stamp tool annotation, but as Okular prompts, "Experimental feature | Stamps inserted in PDF documents are not visible in PDF readers other than Okular".)

The reason why the annotations don't appear in Inkscape may be the way the Poppler library as used by Okular adds annotations to the PDF, see [Poppler issue 839](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/poppler/poppler/-/issues/839) "Annotations not shown in some other readers because we don't save appearance streams". This is apparently why many of these Okular annotations don't appear in Firefox's built-in PDF.js viewer.

Thanks for a great drawing tool.

From a very unscientific method of spamming the GDB backtrace while opening a ~10 MB file, there were a few main things that popped up:

 - ~15%: other stuff

Let's assume this dodgy method does indeed reflect how much time is being spent in them, though obviously this could be very wrong.

Why are these UTF-8 functions being called then? Let's take a simple example:

```cpp
const Glib::ustring foo = "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet";
if (foo != "bar") {
    std::cout << "Is this fast?";
}
```

Now you're probably thinking, this is pretty fast right? All we need to do is compare the string lengths, figure that they're obviously not equal and move on.

This _would_ be true if these were mere `std::string`s, but alas! Welcome to UTF-8. All of a sudden this becomes particularly expensive when we're dealing with `Glib::ustring`s, because you can't just count the number of bytes to find the number of characters!

`Glib::ustring` performs a linguistically aware comparison instead of a byte by byte one, but most of the time we don't need this.

So is this a valid concern? Here's what I'd suggest, but I'm open to other ideas:

 - If you want to use `==` or `compare` but don't need Unicode comparison, convert it to `std::string` first.
 - If you're not going to be iterating through Unicode strings, consider whether you really need `Glib::ustring`.

Issue:
Snapping to grid is too weak
#### Summary:

* My use case is that I create designs for things like mosaic tilings where I want to create things which are (a) tessellations and (b) the shapes have standard sizes using fixed measuring units.
* Snap to grid should mean precisely that. The page should be divided by the grid into a number of cells and the position and size of every shape drawn when grid snapping is enabled should be defined according to which grid points the key points of the shape lie on. (This sounds more complicated than it is.) Everything that's drawn should be "on the grid". This is the common meaning of aligning things to a grid.
* Snap to grid in Inkscape doesn't currently mean snapping so that every position lies on a grid point. It currently means that sometimes it'll snap to grid points but other times it'll treat grid lines as though they were guide lines, and at other times still it just won't snap the shape to anything at all.
* Inkscape decides these things using concepts internal to itself which the user has no control over and the existence of some of them can only be inferred indirectly (either through their effects or by reading documentation for older versions of the product where UI settings are described which no longer exist).
* These "hidden" elements are:
  * The two distinct concepts of a "grid intersection" and a "grid line" which appear differently in infotips yet only a single option appears in the snapping controls relating to grids and it's unclear which of these two things the option is referring to or how the user is supposed to disable snapping to one of them without disabling snapping to other.
  * The requirement that in order to effect a snap the pointer needs to be within a certain maximum distance from the grid point the user wants to snap to, the "tolerance". The existence of the tolerance, how big it is, or how to change it are unclear.

#### Steps to reproduce:

- Open Inkscape.
- Open Document Properties.
- Create a rectangular grid
- Ensure snapping to grids is enabled.
- Zoom in.
- Select the rectangle tool.
- Draw a rectangle.

#### What happened?

One of three things happens with respect to each of the two points which are used to define the rectangle, depending on the positions of the mouse pointer with respect to the boundaries of the nearest enclosing grid cells:

1. The correct thing happens. I.e. each corner snaps to the point on the grid which was nearest to where the mouse pointer was located (or as Inkscape calls them "grid intersections"). Here's a screenshot where one corner is snapped correctly but the other 3 corners are not. I probably took the screenshot during a move operation but the behaviour is the same during shape creation. https://pasteboard.co/SeR1HUOFhnnT.png
2. One or both points snap to places which lie along a grid line but are not points on the grid. In this case we no longer have a functioning grid coordinate system but rather the grid is acting as though it were a whole bunch of guides placed at regular intervals horizontally and vertically. In this case Inkscape tells you that it's snapping to a "grid line" which it treats as a distinctly different semantic concept from a "grid intersection". https://pasteboard.co/g2Bs4ulruLT4.png
3. One or both both points don't snap to anything because the mouse pointer was placed too far away from any of the grid lines or grid intersections according to some hidden tolerance factor which doesn't seem to be adjustable from anywhere in the UI.

#### What should have happened?

* It should be possible to create designs using grids in such a way that everything is locked to the grid.
* If snapping to "grid lines" at places which aren't "grid intersections" is a thing that some people want then snapping to grid lines and snapping to grid intersections need to be listed as two separate items on the advanced snapping menu so that they enabled or disabled separately. https://pasteboard.co/nPjRdk0vokVh.png (Though what it would mean to enable snapping to grid lines but simultaneously disable snapping to grid intersections I don't know, since in mathematics a point has zero area.)
* It should be possible to increase or decrease the overall snapping tolerance in general.
* In the case of snapping to the grid it should be possible (but optional) to override the general tolerance with an "infinite" tolerance while grids are displayed, thus guaranteeing that no matter how far away something is placed from a grid intersection it will always snap to a point on the grid (AKA grid intersection).

#### Workaround

After messing about with this for a whole day, tearing my hair out, discussing it in the forum with people who didn't seem to get why this would be a problem (https://inkscape.org/forums/beyond/how-to-restore-previous-grid-snapping-behaviour/), searching the web and confirming that older versions of Inkscape contained the features that I need, finding something called gridtolerance inside my preferences.xml file which unfortunately seems to be non-functional, and then finally searching through the source code and following a trail of interesting clues, I finally discovered that the following steps will activate a hidden feature that works (for now).

1. Open the XML editor.
2. Find something called namedview1.
3. Add an attribute called gridtolerance and set its value to 65535.

It really shouldn't be this hard to set up a basic grid based design though!

(Unfortunately I'm a JavaScript person rather than a competent C++ or GTK programmer, so I didn't get as far a putting together a pull request.)

#### Summary:

When changing the selected layer in the new dialogue, Inkscape now changes the selection to the group that layer represents instead of keeping the previous selection.

I used to use this a lot to change the context of tools like "select and transform" to the root context of the level when working with nested groups so I do things like select a few objects, change the focus to the layer, set opacity on the layer to 100%, and then use the colour picker to set the fill/stroke of the objects selected.

- open Inkscape

After following the steps the selection is changed to the entirety of layer 1 (not all the shapes inside layer 1, just layer 1)

The single object from layer 2 that was selected before switching layers should be the only thing selected.

Issue:
Pasting as "Multiple of grid spacing" doesn't align properly; X and Y coords are rounded to an integer number of pixels instead
#### Summary:
When pasting an objects, its X and Y coords are rounded to an integer number of pixels, even when the grid is active.
This breaks the "Paste as a multiple of grid spacing" functionality, which was very useful when making more "technical" drawings such as schematics / diagrams that are meant to be aligned with the grid at regular intervals; the rounding causes the pasted object to be misaligned by half the edge width (or up to half a pixel).

#### Cause:
This regression was probably introduced in inkscape!5160 which explicitly introduces a rounding of the pasted coordinates.

The rationale for that change was that *randomly* pasted objects (freely; not specifically aligned to a grid or pasted in place (see inkscape!5477)) should be aligned to a whole pixel offset in order to reduce aliasing artifacts (when displayed on a pixel screen at a 1:1 ratio).

This is a valid reasoning in my opinion so the developers may want to consider keeping this behavior, but it should be subject to the following conditions:
* The grid is disabled.
  If it is enabled, the alignment should adjust to the grid.
* The rounding should apply to the **offset,** not the destination's absolute position.
  In other words, **disabling the grid should effectively work as enabling a 1px grid.**
  This makes more sense than aligning the copies but leaving the original unaligned, results in identical aliasing artifacts on the pasted object as on the original (when displayed at a 1:1 scale), and allows the user to fine-tune the pixel offset of the original to achieve the desired effect (which may focus on internal lines of the object rather than the bounding box) and then have all copies replicate that effect.

(This probably means that the behavior should be implemented in `multipleOfGridPitch()` itself rather than in the pasting function.)

#### Steps to reproduce:
- Started with a blank Inkscape profile (set INKSCAPE_PROFILE_DIR=C:\tmp\inkscape-home, also tried adding LANG=C, LC_ALL=C, LC_NUMERIC=C, LANGUAGE=)
- New document
- Enable grid (#) (defaults to millimetric (not a multiple of 1 px), but also reproducible with px grids)
- Enable snapping (%)
- Select rectangle tool (r)
- Fill: gray, stroke: black (or to taste; but make sure you enable stroke)
- Draw a small rectangle with both corners aligned to grid (snap tooltip: "Handle to grid intersection").
- If your grid spacing is a multiple of 1 px, ensure the rectangle stroke width is not an exact multiple of 2 px (1 px is fine)
- Observe that the resulting rectangle is indeed aligned with the grid (zoom in if necessary): grid lines run along the edges exactly through the middle
- Copy rectangle (Ctrl-C)
- Paste rectangle elsewhere (Ctrl-V) (snap tooltip: "Multiple of grid spacing")
- Zoom in to 1600% or so, so that you can clearly see the alignment of the pasted rectangle edge [*]
- Select selector tool (s)
- Set units from "mm" to "px" on the toolbar
- Observe the X and Y values for the pasted rectangle [**]

#### What SHOULD have happened:
1. The middle line of the edge is aligned with the grid (half the edge width to either side) [*]
2. X and Y coordinates are not a whole number of pixels, but a multiple of the grid minus half the edge width [**]
    (for example, if grid spacing = 10 px and edge width = 1 px, the X and Y coords will always end in "xxx9.500")

#### What happened:
1. The middle line of the edge is NOT aligned with the grid [*]
2. X and Y coordinates are always an exact multiple of 1 px [**]
    (end in ".000", or sometimes ".999" probably due to rounding errors)

This looks like a regression; it didn't happen in earlier versions of Inkscape I have used (e.g. 1.0) - there the pasted object always had an offset that was a multiple of the grid.

Issue:
Relink to Copied always moves according to transform
Migrated from: https://bugs.launchpad.net/inkscape/+bug/251365

#### Summary:
Inkscape offers 3 preference options about how to move clones and linked offsets when their original is moved. All 3 preferences work correctly when dealing directly with clones and linked offsets. The preferences are: 

**Moving original: clones and linked offsets**

* Move in parallel
* Stay unmoved
* Move according to transform

Where it **doesn't work** is the **Relink to copied** command on a cloned object. 

If a clone is being relinked to a copied object it will **ALWAYS** be moved according to transform, even if the preferences have it set to move in parallel or to stay unmoved.  

![EXPECTATIONScreenshot_from_2020-09-04_01-15-26](/uploads/ad800c9e66ca5649f54e6e0b8617e724/EXPECTATIONScreenshot_from_2020-09-04_01-15-26.png)

#### Steps to reproduce:
1. Make sure that in Inkscape Preferences > Behavior > Clones you have ticked either **Move in parallel** or **Stay unmoved** (I chose Stay unmoved)
2. Create an object
3. Clone the object 
1. Move the clone away for better visibility, I moved to the right
4. Rotate the clone to make the behaviour "move according to transform" more visible
4. Duplicate the original object
5. Move the duplicate (anywhere, I chose downwards)
6. Copy the duplicate (Ctrl+C)
1. Select the cloned object
7. Edit > Clone > Relink to Copied

#### What happened?

The clone was relinked but it moved according to the way the duplicate was moved (in my case downwards and to the right) when it shouldn't have moved at all. 

![RESULTScreenshot_from_2020-09-04_01-14-26](/uploads/b85a6a42e6bb62b270bae0c1006c0b4e/RESULTScreenshot_from_2020-09-04_01-14-26.png)

#### What should have happened?

Relink to Copied should respect the chosen option about moving clones from Inkscape preferences. 

If the preference is set to `Move in parallel` the relinked clone should move to the position that is parallel to the object it was relinked to. 

If the preference is set to `Stay unmoved` the relinked clone shouldn't move at all. 

![EXPECTATIONScreenshot_from_2020-09-04_01-15-26](/uploads/950b4c5aba3eefccd00375a1aee447b1/EXPECTATIONScreenshot_from_2020-09-04_01-15-26.png)

> This happens because we are being a little lazy. The current approach to pattern rendering is to calculate the size of the pattern tile based on the size of the pattern on the screen and render it to an image surface. However, if the tile is very large and based on e.g. an upscaled bitmap, we end up allocating a giant image for no reason and filling it with lots of interpolated data.
> 
> The fix would be to have a limit on the size of the allocated tile, e.g. 5MB. If this threshold is exceeded, we should switch to a different rendering strategy. Instead of rendering the entire tile to an image surface, we should just repeatedly draw it on the target surface inside a group. This group should then be composited using a mask based on the object's fill / stroke area. Unfortunately, this might cause some problems with seams at the edges of the tile.

Issue:
Swatch disappears on original object when deleting clones
#### Summary:
In specific circumstances involving an object with a swatch applied, which is cloned multiple times, will have its swatch removed when the clones are deleted.

#### Steps to reproduce:
1. open Inkscape, new file
2. Create a text object, with no stroke and a fill using a swatch (just click the swatch icon)
3. Create a rectangle with no fill and any stroke
4. Group the text and rectangle
5. Clone the group
6. Duplicate the clone twice
7. Delete all three clones
8. Toggle layer visibility off and on (to force a redraw)

#### What happened?

The original text is no longer visible.

#### What should have happened?

The text should still be visible.
...

Sample attachments:

![drawing.svg](/uploads/488d44d6aba3f9ab0eac43284e276741/drawing.svg)

This file was created between step 4. and 5. Saving a file after step 6. cannot reproduce the problem, unless you delete both clones, undo that, and delete both clones again, so it seems to happen only when at least one (it seems) clone has been created in the current inkscape session.

Some additional observations:
 - The swatch is implemented using a `fill` style that refers to a first `linearGradient` object, with a `href` pointing to a second `linearGradient`. When multiple objects use the same swatch, they share the second `linearGradient`, but each have a unique first `linearGradient` (so the first one links the object to the second, the actual swatch that also carries the swatch name).
 - When this problem happens, this first `linearGradient` object is deleted, making the original text object's `fill` style refer to a non-exist id.
 - Cloning the text directly, or omitting the rect from the group prevents reproducing the problem.
 - Making two clones (instead of duplicating the first clone) does not seem to reproduce the problem.
 - A swatch applied to another rect instead of a text does not show the problem, so this seems to be text-specific somehow.
 - This also happens when undo-ing, e.g. select two clones (that seems sufficient), duplicate them, undo, and the problem occurs.
 - Reproducing is prettty reliable, though sometimes it is also a bit unexpected (it seems I need one clone and two duplicates directly after loading the sample file, but after some duplicating and undo'ing, just one clone and one duplicate seems sufficient).
 - The problem also occurs when deleting the clones one by one (sometimes already when deleting two of them).

Issue:
OpenGL mode problems due to GTK3 bugs
## Description

This is a meta-issue tracking the known problems in OpenGL mode on various platforms that are due to GTK3 bugs. Before filing a bug report about performance problems or glitching, please check if it's documented here first, as it's more than likely to be an upstream issue. Although some workarounds are given, these issues aren't expected to be fixable until after the [GTK4 port](https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/merge_requests/6039).

#### Steps to reproduce:

* Open Inkscape.
* Enable Preferences > Rendering > Developer mode > Enable OpenGL.
* Attempt to use Inkscape.

## Platform status

Here are the known issues on the various platforms.

#### Linux + Wayland

This appears to be the most stable platform out of the box, with only one known issue:

* Issue: During continuous mouse input, there is a slightly increased tendency to drop frames. This means that dragging objects or panning is subtly more stuttery than in Cairo mode.
* Workaround: None known.

#### Linux + X11

Surprisingly for such a widely-used platform, there are several crippling performance bugs. Fortunately, full workarounds exist, and when enabled, this is actually the best-performing platform.

* Issue: All operations (dragging, panning, zooming) are extremely laggy. Sometimes, long periods can go by without any screen refresh.
* Workaround: Forcing the environment variable `GDK_RENDERING=image` seems to fix most of the problem. Alternatively, use a [patched GTK/GDK](https://gitlab.gnome.org/pbs3141/gtk/-/commit/267fb8b9989a1cdd77d5dde2b26fac4f593ed2e1) which includes this and some more changes. This may eventually be [fixed upstream](https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/gtk/-/merge_requests/6042).

* Issue: While resizing, there are artifacts consisting of old screen content. After resize, the screen flickers between the current and previous frames when the mouse is moved.
* Workaround: None known, but the artifacts disappear after the next interaction with the canvas (e.g. scroll).

#### macOS

The problems with GTK3 on the Mac are well-known (see #1614), and are magnified further in OpenGL mode. However, @NPJ2000 reports that a custom build with recent dependencies works perfectly.

* Issue: Window is completely black.
* Workaround: force the environment variables `GDK_GL=always` and `GDK_RENDERING=image`.

* Issue: Even with the above workaround, Inkscape is unusable with missing updates on scroll/zoom, full-screen blue glitching on resize, and screwed up coordinate transformations. (But at least it's really fast! :upside_down:)
* Workaround: None known.

#### Windows

The situation with GTK on Windows varies between X11 and MacOS, depending on luck:

* Issue: Dragging objects may be slower than in Cairo mode - this seems to fluctuate wildly over time with changing dependencies.
* Workaround: None known.

* Issue: Crashes instantly upon enabling OpenGL. This comes and goes at random as GTK add and remove bugs - [first time](https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/merge_requests/4133#note_1036492567), [second time](https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/issues/4031#note_1231295420).
* Workaround: Copy-paste a working version of the GTK/GDK DLLs from an older version.

* Issue: Fullscreen mode is broken (https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inbox/-/issues/8908).
* Workaround: None known.

Issue:
Investigate existing instances of a Glib::ustring being sent to a stringstream, and floats/doubles converted to strings
Follow-up to https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/merge_requests/4335

If we send a Glib::ustring to a stream (like std::ostringstream or std::cerr), we risk throwing an exception on some machines (like Window machines or some machines where locale is not set at all or is set to ANSI).

Examples of previous errors:
- https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/issues/3027 (error messages may contain unicode, like the quotation marks)
-  https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/issues/3473 (translated strings contain unicode)

I know at least one instance still exists, `SpinButtonToolItem::create_numeric_menu_item` still sends a translated Glib::ustring label to `std::ostringstream ss;` (this occurs with the star toolbar when the window is shrunk). Changing it to `ss << ": " << label << Glib::ustring("لا شيء");` can throw an exception.

I haven't checked for other instances (or if a crash/freeze pops up in an existing language with the above instance).

A fix can be made, similar to https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/merge_requests/4335.  
A bunch were tackled in https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/merge_requests/4699

----------

Follow up to !3575

Bonus work would be to investigate existing instances where we send floats to stringstream or otherwise converting it to a string without making sure the decimal separator will be printed as a `.`. This may break in a German locale (or other locales that use comma (,) decimal separators).

Funnily enough, a similar issue to !3575 just popped up, in https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/issues/3240 . Copying what I mentioned there

> A more thorough search with `g_strdup_printf.+%[\d\.+-]*f` turns up ~~src/extension/internal/pov-out.cpp~~ (unaffected/commented out, and uses `g_ascii_formatd` instead) and `BasicWriter::writeFloat` and `BasicWriter::writeDouble` in src/io/stream/inkscapestream.cpp
> 
> Those BasicaWriter calls are currently unused and I'm a bit hesitant to touch them. If you were, you'd probably use `g_ascii_formatd` though

(I also searched for `g_strdup_printf.+%[\d\.+-]*[efgEFG]` too)

Issue:
Problems with font libraries during static destruction
Following on from the discussion at https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/merge_requests/4702#note_1077391161, this issue documents a crash in `FontFactory` that is currently being hackily worked around, which would be good to solve properly.

### Description

`FontFactory` is singleton object that manages the interactions with various system font libraries, such as FreeType, Pango and Harfbuzz. It currently deliberately leaks itself at program exit to avoid running its destructor, because doing so would crash:

```c++
FontFactory &FontFactory::get()
{
    // FIXME: This intentionally leaks at program exit. It is a workaround for the fact the
    // destructor crashes at program exit due to Pango being unloaded first.
    static auto factory = new FontFactory();
    return *factory;
}
```

The reason for the crash is that the FreeType library is destroyed first, before the `FontFactory` destructor, so since the destructor calls into FreeType, this results in a crash.

You might say it's no surprise things like this are happening - the destructor of `FontFactory` runs after `main()` during static destruction, and libraries are also unloaded after `main()`, so this is definitely asking for trouble. But actually it should be fine: first all statics are destroyed, then all shared libraries are unloaded, and you can check this is happening. #### Version info

I've only reproduced the crash on 1.3 dev, but the valgrind error happens on 1.2.1 too, and I believe this bug could go back quite a while.

#### Theory

Caveat: my `valgrind` has been half-broken for a while and won't show debug symbols for my debug build, so the following is based on bad information:

* The assertion suggests a missing decrement of `SPObject::hrefcount`. But logging all increments/decrements to `hrefcount` shows that they match. The only explanation is that `hrefcount` is being overwritten through a pointer to a freed object.
* This prompted the use of `valgrind`, which did indeed show memory errors, through not the smoking gun of a write-after-free. This is because my valgrind log was of the non-crash case. I bet you could catch a crash and write-after-free with enough patience though.
* From the valgrind log (as I commented in it), I think the problem is SPStyle refcounting.

  `SPObject`s typically hold an `SPStyle` whose lifetime is contained within that of the `SPObject`. But `SPStyle` supports reference counting, which allows other users to hold a ref on the `SPStyle` to extend its lifetime beyond that of the `SPObject`. Thus, the `SPStyle` can end up being destroyed much later than the `SPObject` if someone holds a ref for too long. The problem with that is `SPStyle` is rife with pointers back to the associated `SPObject`. For a start, it has the `object` member variable. It also has various subobjects with back pointers. The one I'm concerned about is this one, a URIReference, from `style-internal.cpp`:

  ```c++
  value.href = new SPPaintServerReference(style->object);
  ```

  The function `sp_style_object_release` only takes care of nulling the `object` pointer when the object is destructed. It does not make sure all the object pointers within subobjects are nulled too. So that leaves it possible for an `SPStyle` to get destructed after its `SPObject`, causing the above URIReference to access the freed `SPObject` in its destructor. This is what appears to be going on in the valgrind log. Furthermore, I intentionally made `SPStyle` leak, causing its destructor to never be called, and the crash went away.

  I believe the whole `SPStyle` refcounting system is rotten for this reason. It gives a false sense of security that holding a reference to a `SPStyle` solves all memory problems. In reality, it leads to crashes because `SPStyle` does not expect to have its lifetime to be extended in this way. I've previously encountered such crashes while working on https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/merge_requests/4556, for example.

  The text layout engine does exactly this (see `sp_style_ref(style);` in `Layout::appendText`). In fact, it's the **only** remaining place in the code that does this. So I think this pretty well implicates SPStyle refcounting as being the root of the problem here. Given the text layout engine is the only remaining use, it would be great to fix this bug by refactoring out SPStyle refcounting completely. (/cc @Tavmjong)

#### What happened?

It reports the version as `1.2.2-`.

#### What should have happened?

It should have reported the version as `1.2.2`.

I believe the dash is to accommodate INKSCAPE_VERSION_SUFFIX when there is one, e.g. `1.2.2-dev`, but this case it is the official release and should not have a dash.

The version used here by Windows comes from the registry, and is probably populated by the installer.

```
PS C:\> Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\Inkscape\' | Select DisplayName, DisplayVersion | format-list

DisplayName    : Inkscape
DisplayVersion : 1.2.2-
```

This issue is also causing problems with [winget](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-cli), Microsoft's new command line package manger, as it always reports the installed version with a trailing dash, prompting you to update even if you have the latest version. To my understanding this is the correct behavior by winget, as per Semantic Versioning 2.0.0, versions with a hyphen denote pre-release version; therefor `1.2.2` should be greater then `1.2.2-` ([ref](https://semver.org/#spec-item-9)).

Issue:
The stroke is cut off or cropped if filter (e.g. blur) applied
#### Summary:
The outline of an object made of strokes is cut off at the geometry (middle or vertex) of the stroke instead of at the thickness of the stroke. Converting stroke to path (so it doesn't have a stroke, but uses fills instead) fixes this as the filter region is relative to the geometric bounding box (see fixed file).

#### Steps to reproduce:

- open Inkscape
- Choose "Draw freehand lines"
- Draw a 4-sided object with wavy edges, drawing the four edges separately, making sure the corner is red before starting or ending a line, so they continue where the last line left off.
- Click a color to set the fill
- Set stroke style thick such as 4 mm
- Add a small blur

Note in stable releases (1.0.1 and earlier), it is easy to accidentally add a blur when scrolling (as has occurred here, see https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inbox/-/issues/4197)

#### What happened?

The edges are cut off as the automatic filter region does not take stroke-width into account.

#### What should have happened?

Filter region should account for the stroke-width, so the entire thickness of the stroke is displayed.

Issue:
Connector spacing changes in XML editor not immediate in second document
#### Summary:
You can modify the Connector spacing directly in the XML editor. However, if the first document is closed so a new document replaces it, these changes are *only* visible after reopening the file.

#### Steps to reproduce:
<!-- Describe what you did (step-by-step) so we can reproduce: -->

1. open Inkscape
1. create a rectangle
1. switch to the connectors tool
1. with the rectangle selected, click the first toolbar button (Make connectors avoid selected objects)
1. click outside the rectangle and draw a line that passes through the rectangle (the line should go around the rectangle)
1. increase the spacing value (in the toolbar)
1. open the xml editor
1. select the sodipodi:namedview element
1. change `inkscape:connector-spacing` (make the change large, e.g. 5 to 50)
1. close the document and repeat steps 2 to 9

#### What happened?
- steps 2-9 are optional, but show that the connectors update when changing spacing
    - when repeating these steps after closing the document, these **connectors do not update** till you save and reopen the file
- when the above bug happens, the spacing value in the toolbar isn't updated by XML editor changes anymore

Note: this bug doesn't happen if the new document doesn't replace the old one (and opens in a new window instead)

![inkscape-minor-connector](/uploads/eec15ac7113449b548ed2cc1289ebab9/inkscape-minor-connector.mp4)

#### What should have happened?
- closing document doesn't change behaviour.

#### Misc

Found while investigating https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/merge_requests/2616,

The signals that track changes to spacing are created https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/blob/fdf98dce7073cbeeaef7a060796715be5cea81ea/src/ui/toolbar/connector-toolbar.cpp#L170-181 (note the first statement is never true and does nothing). These are not removed, and no new signals created after the first document is closed.

#### Version Info:
- Inkscape 1.1-dev (fdf98dce70, 2020-12-15) Linux Mint 20
- Inkscape 0.92.5 (0ad1ac969f, 2020-08-06) Linux Mint 20

Classify as SMELL or NO_SMELL based on whether it describes architectural problems.

Issue:
Mirror symmetry LPE: Weird drag-handling of mirror line
#### Summary:
Dragging the mirror line of the Mirror Symmetry LPE behaves weirdly when changing modes.

This was originally reported as part of https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inbox/-/issues/3814, but moved to its own commit for easier tracking.

#### Steps to reproduce:

* Create a new file, draw a path, add Mirror Symmetry LPE.
* Use the edit paths tool to see the mirror line vertically to the right of the drawing.
* Switch to mode "Y coordinate of mirror line midpoint"
* See that the centerpoint is unchanged, but the start/end Y coordinate are set to the centerpoint Y coordinate and the X coordinate to the left/rightmost X coordinate of the drawing. This means that the centerpoint is no longer in the center between the start and endpoint (in this case, the endpoint and the centerpoint even end up in the same place), which is confusing. Also note that the XML is unchanged, only the displayed positions (in the drawing and the path effects panel) are updated.
* In this mode, the start/endpoints cannot be dragged. Dragging the centerpoint makes its X coordinate jump to the midpoint of the start/end points, and now only the Y coordinate can be changed by dragging.

#### What should have happened?
This could be fixed by updating the center X coordinate to be halfway the start and end when switching to this mode. This could be problematic when repeatedly switching modes would then cause the centerpoint to move around the drawing, but in practice the XML is not actually updated until you actually drag or change the coordinates, so putting the centerpoint in the center would be for display only, which makes sense.

A related improvement could be to rename the "Y coordinate of mirror line midpoint" mode to something like "Horizontal line through mirror line midpoint" (which makes it more consistent with the other options, and you're not so much mirror across an Y coordinate, but a horizontal line).

- Pango version: 1.44.7
- Operating System: Ubuntu

```

Issue:
Support multiple user-defined connection points on objects
### Background

To be a true contender for engineering use (especially electrical engineering), Inkscape must support multiple user-defined connectors on objects. Logic gates (such as AND and OR gates) and transistors have multiple pins, thus requiring multiple connection pins. Other disciplines have similar symbols and requirements.

Microsoft Visio continues to be the industry standard for schematic work. Inkscape would be a contender **if it had this feature**.

Example Visio drawing with schematic symbols: [connectors.vsdx](/uploads/b426660cb7f07c93d2460c7eceb33db8/connectors.vsdx)

### Details

I can provide more examples upon request.

Visio provides the two tools specific to connectors and connection points:

* The Connector Tool (right-angled lines) is used to create and modify point-to-point connections.
* The Connection Point Tool (blue X) is used to create, modify, remove the connection points themselves.

#### 01_connector_tool.gif

* When the Pointer Tool (arrow) is active, connection points are not shown.
* When the Connector Tool (right-angled lines) is active, connection points are shown when the pointer is near them.
* The Connector Tool allows you to make new connections or change existing connections.

![01_connector_tool](/uploads/b1fb9c5e538c6b347d788b37e01ccfb6/01_connector_tool.gif)

#### 02_connector_overlap.gif
* When two connectors are connected to the same pin, the pin of the selected connector is the one that will be moved when you select and drag.
* Visio automatically puts half-circle overlap "hops" on the horizontal connector when two connectors overlap.
* This "hop" property can be enabled or disabled on a per-object basis.

![02_connector_overlap](/uploads/eeda49da5c670b1d641e58a24b0b6b07/02_connector_overlap.gif)

#### 03_connector_rerouting.gif
* Connectors have span control points, located at the middle of each span, that allow you to adjust the routing.
* When a span control point is moved and one end of the span is constrained (such as connected to a connection point), a new route jog is added. (This is an important behavior to implement.)
* Visio adds and removes (simplifies) the route spans as needed.
* Span adjustment respects any snapping features that are enabled.

![03_connector_rerouting](/uploads/d1e655d024d8def2b1f2dcc18af95970/03_connector_rerouting.gif)

#### 04_object_movement.gif
* When objects are moved, Visio tries to preserve the routes of associated connectors as much as possible, to minimize disturbance to previously made route adjustments.

![04_object_movement](/uploads/40eca215b1058e69bed8fe87ef5043e0/04_object_movement.gif)

#### 05_modifying_connection_points.gif
* The Connection Point tool allows you to see and modify the connection points on the selected object.
* To select a connection point, click on it; the selected connection point turns red. Multiple connection points can be shift-selected.
* Pressing Del will delete the selected connection point(s).
* To add a new connection point, Ctrl-click where desired. Visio snaps to guides and geometries to help place the point.
* For complex or curved objects, sometimes I draw temporary "helper" lines to snap the connection point to an intersection.

![05_modifying_connection_points](/uploads/9df2d7330dc57ae77bb4080af8de1e0d/05_modifying_connection_points.gif)

#### 06_connection_points_and_grouping.gif
* The Connection Point tool can apply connection points to groups.
* When a group is ungrouped, its connection points disappear but the connection points on its children remain intact.

![06_connection_points_and_grouping](/uploads/8f80d5849be4e248e193cac38a0efac0/06_connection_points_and_grouping.gif)

#### 07_connection_points_selected_obj.gif
* With the Connection Point tool, Ctrl-click *always* adds the connection point to the currently selected object (relative to its position).

![07_connection_points_selected_obj](/uploads/cfd3d56be819fc23b23156ce603b601c/07_connection_points_selected_obj.gif)

#### 08_pointer_tool_connectors.gif
* The Pointer Tool (arrow) is not specific to connectors or connection points.
* But as a convenience, the Pointer Tool allows connectors to be reconnected, rerouted, or moved entirely.
* When a connector is moved in its entirety with the Pointer Tool, it tries to connect to existing connection points at the new location.
* Only the Pointer Tool moves a connector in its entirety; the Connector Tool does not.

![08_pointer_tool_connectors](/uploads/9d575782008e4c6d9032d7c36e49644a/08_pointer_tool_connectors.gif)

Issue:
Evaluate which languages to use when matching `sytemLanguage` attribute for rendering
The [`systemLanguage`](https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG11/struct.html#ConditionalProcessingSystemLanguageAttribute) attribute can be used to conditionally render elements in a language most suitable for the user.

* The code for matching currently is in [`evaluateSystemLanguage()`](https://inkscape.gitlab.io/inkscape/doxygen/conditions_8cpp.html#a0cd7997e939bdfc9f0db58a93888b95b)
* The languages that are used for matching are currently a document property and evaluated in [`getLanguages()`](https://inkscape.gitlab.io/inkscape/doxygen/classSPDocument.html#aca565ea8bea2102bbbf44ff54b84c4fd)

The SVG spec is brief as to what languages should be considered as suitable for the user in this matching. It simply speaks of *"user preferences"* without expanding on how the user is supposed to indicate them.

Inkscape historically considers the "language" field specified in RDF and the POSIX locale of the system, which might or might not be the correct thing to do (see [related discussion](https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/merge_requests/3147#note_565327512)).

A core question is if this matching should be document-specific at all (i.e. if things like RDF "language" or the `xml:lang` attribute need to be considered), or if `getLanguages()` should be dropped altogether.


_**Note: This issue is NOT about enabling users to edit different languages (which will be a separate feature request that also needs UX work). This issue is specifically about the rendering aspects.**_

| Export format | Code |

Checking the path with the XML edit reveals that `image.png` (located in `Desktop/testfolder/image.png`, the SVG is stored in the same folder became `../../Desktop/testfolder/image.png`. That's one `../` too many. Running the extension again adds another `../`. When there's enough `../`-s in front of the path to reach the root directory of the hard drive, the path is converted to an absolute path (`file:///Desktop/testfolder/image.png`), which also doesn't exist.

#### What should have happened?

Relative paths should be kept.

> Apparently, all the xlink:href attributes of the document are converted to absolute links by Script::solve_reldir (in src/extensions/implementation/script.cpp) so that the scripts can use them. But they don't get their relative value when the script is terminated.

> The links of the <image> elements are converted to relative by rebase_hrefs (in src/xml/rebase-hrefs.cpp) when saving the document, but nothing is done for <a> elements. #### Steps to reproduce:
<!-- Describe what you did (step-by-step) so we can reproduce: -->

- open Inkscape
- use the Bezier tool (B) to create a line
- open Fill and Stroke (Shift+Ctrl+F) -> Stroke style (Alt+Y) -> Markers
- under "Markers", assign any marker or arrow head to the line
- duplicate the line (Ctrl+D)

#### What happened?

Inkscape duplicates the line and **also** duplicates the marker definition:

![image](/uploads/2ee9909b2f207a6d02d05fc312357875/image.png)

![image](/uploads/25ec89f4ab1186026148e6011d134126/image.png)

**Edit:** *Astonishingly enough this only happens when the Fill and Stroke panel is open (regardless of which of its pages is active). If the Fill and Stroke panel is closed when the duplicate is made, the duplicate line (correctly) references the original's marker defs.*

In and of itself this doesn't matter too much (aside from bloating the document with redundancy).

But it has an awkward side effect – it also bloats the line marker drop-down box with loads of redundant markers (to the point of making it nearly unusable in large documents):

![image](/uploads/b04325c5be39e260687b604e6547f723/image.png)

(In the large drawing I'm currently working on, I have several screenfuls of identical markers a the top of the marker drop-down by now.)

#### What should have happened?

Inkscape should have used the original's marker definition (in the sample above, `#Arrow1Send`).

As a mitigation, File -> Clean Up Document should detect redundant marker definitions and unify them into one.

TESTED
Inkscape 1.0 (4035a4fb49, 2020-05-01) and Inkscape 0.92 --- both of them crash.

- Windows 10 (up to date in patches)

The PDF load window with thumbnail should display.

Issue:
External `<use>` elements don't reference external elements correctly (only checks including document's defs)
Note: this is cross-posted from https://inkscape.org/forums/beyond/embedded-svg-does-not-display-markers/ - I have cross-posted it here because 1) this may be a bug in 0.92, <strike>and 2) when I try to open `foo.svg` in Inkscape 1.0 beta, Inkscape crashes (which is definitely a bug)</strike> Edit: crash fixed, bug in 0.92 still occurs in 1.0

It was also reported in https://bugs.launchpad.net/inkscape/+bug/1777984  

#### Steps to replicate
1. Open [foo.svg](https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inbox/uploads/3c57ab2c85058a26271250de1c3a64ad/foo.svg) in inkscape (contains a `<use>` that references the root element of `bar.svg`
2. Compare to [bar.svg](https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inbox/uploads/b49a05219c82a7b6c0bde1365764a3ae/bar.svg) in Inkscape (contains elements that have markers. These markers are defined in the `<defs>` of `bar.svg`)

#### What happened?
- the marker don't display in `foo.svg`, but do when `bar.svg` is opened directly.

Generally, what is happening is that
- If your document has a `<use>` element that references an element from a separate document, use directives or markers (basically just links) in that external document will not function properly (except for further external <use> elements).
- The links in the external document will match the original document instead (if there is a matching id)
- Even if the xlink:hrefs in the external document refer to elements that are nested within the <use>'d entity, those will not function correctly.

#### What should have happened?
- the marker should have displaced
- more generally, `<use>` elements should deeply clone the contents of the referenced element (see https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG11/struct.html#UseElement). Thus links inside the referenced elements should still work.

```

Issue:
Newly created Autoflowed text shouldn't receive parent transformations
<!--
    See our full bug reporting guidelines at https://inkscape.org/contribute/report-bugs/
    Writing a good bug report will ensure we'll be able to help efficiently. 🙂
-->

#### Summary:
<!-- Summarize the issue/suggestion concisely: -->

New additions to a group should not be affected by previous transformations of that group. They are. Kinda seems like this is part of a category of 1.0 bugs that attempted to optimize the XML but didn't account for all the ramifications.


#### Steps to reproduce:
<!-- Describe what you did (step-by-step) so we can reproduce: -->

It's maybe easier to get this right if you keep the Objects window open and expanded, and watch both it and the status bar as you go along.

- open Inkscape
- create a rectangle (status bar shows you are on Layer 1)
- Group it (Object->Group) (status bar shows you are on Layer 1)
- Select the group (status bar shows you are on Layer 1)
- Rotate the group 30 or 40 degrees (status bar shows you are on Layer 1)
- Enter the group, e.g. with Ctrl-Enter (status bar shows you are now inside a group)
- Click the text tool (status bar shows you are now inside a group)
- click/drag to create an area of flowed text (status bar shows you are now inside a group)
- Start typing text and immediately see that it is not horizontal, but rotated the same amount you rotated the group
- At this point, Objects window should show you have a group containing a rectangle and text box.
- If you save and examine the file, you should see that the group transformation has been stored as an attribute of the "g" element representing the group, which presumably explains why it modifies the newly added text object


#### What should have happened?

Inkscape should return to pre-1.0 behavior; transforms on the group should not affect objects added to that group later. The current behavior is not WYSIWYG, the user has no clue why their new object is being transformed or how to stop that from happening. Likewise, if the user were to manage to move the new text box outside the group (possible with drag-and-drop in the Objects window), they would see the transformations undone and the text would "pop" back to horizontal, providing more confusion for the user.

#### Probably Contingent Bug:

After you follow the above steps, you should discover that if you select the newly added text object inside your group, the Object->Pop Selected Objects Out of Group menu item will not do anything. If you repeat the above steps but do not transform the group, however, that menu command will work. Hopefully this means it is part of the same bug and doesn't require a separate issue.


#### Version Info:

```
- Inkscape Version: 1.1-dev (608fe7bbae, 2020-07-26), and 1.0 release
- Operating System: Windows 7, final release.
```

#### Summary:

Xfig format remains relevant because, despite its age, Xfig can still run on modern systems (see: <http://mcj.sourceforge.net/>) but it is showing its age. Inkscape is one of the few viable alternative vector graphics editors because it will open Xfig files.

1. Select `File`→`Open...` (`Cmd-O`). The Open dialog is displayed.
1. Select `All files` in the file type filter popup menu in the bottom right of the dialog window.

Failed to load the requested file <path to file>

---

this happens because `PAGE_SIZE` (and `PAGESIZE`) are defined as macros. this makes them trample the c++ namespace, so using them anywhere fails since it just expands to a number or whatnot.

i don't have a reference offhand for if it's valid for them to be macros from headers or not, but it probably is.

Issue:
Drawing a circle from the centre does not work in a useful way
#### Summary:

The Ellipse/Arc Tool can be used to draw a circle from the centre outwards by holding Shift+Ctrl. However, this circle cannot snap to a given point, the mouse cursor is always outside the circle (approximately at a corner of the bounding square), which makes the Ellipse/Arc Tool useless for doing even the most basic [compass & straightedge geometric constructions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Straightedge_and_compass_construction).

#### Steps to reproduce:

Suppose you have a straight line. Let's mark its endpoints C and P:

![image](/uploads/5c5ebf4ffdc788d5746abe6f84b12d16/image.png){width=244 height=232}

Let's try to construct a circle, such that the centre is in the point C, and the point P is on the circle itself. In other words, CP is the radius of the circle. This is the intended result:

![image](/uploads/24faa2daf5704674e876eab0969f7d9b/image.png){width=244 height=232}

This is impossible to do with the Ellipse/Arc tool. Trying to draw a circle from the point C holding down Shift+Control makes it impossible to snap to node P, because the mouse cursor is always outside the circle.

#### Suggestion:

What would make this tool vastly more useful and intuitive is if the mouse cursor stayed on the circumference of the circle while dragging out from the centre. Then it could snap to anywhere and it would be possible to use it like a pair of compasses and do geometric constructions with it.

#### Current workarounds:

To draw the above image, I cheated and did it in reverse: first I drew the circle, then the radius, then removed the circle for the first image.

There is a workaround, but it involves using an experimental path effect called Circle. This is quite buggy: for example, duplicating a line with that path effect causes the effect to not render, requiring one to remove it and add it again. If the Circle path effect is flattened, the circle is now a path object, not an ellipse. However, once these limitations are understood and the user is aware that experimental Path Effects exist, it is a reliable way to draw circles from the centre, as unintuitive as it may be.

Another workaround is using the Measure tool to measure the distance between the two points, then create a circle and input its height and width as the double of that measured value, and then snap it to the point C. This is very, very inconvenient. The Path Effect workaround is much more elegant, but this really ought to be a functionality of the Ellipse/Arc tool. Maybe a separate mode that only works with circles and is used to easily construct a circle defined by two points (like drawing a line).

Issue:
Tiling LPE gap breaks when changing display units
<!--
    See our full bug reporting guidelines at https://inkscape.org/contribute/report-bugs/
    Writing a good bug report will ensure we'll be able to help efficiently. 🙂
-->

#### Summary:
<!-- Summarize the issue/suggestion concisely: -->

The `Tiling` Live Path Effect's `Gap` distances are not updated correctly when the document's display units are changed. This can lead to the appearance of the document changing unexpectedly on subsequent edit or export.

#### Steps to reproduce:
<!-- Describe what you did (step-by-step) so we can reproduce: -->

1. Open Inkscape
2. Create a shape
3. Add a `Tiling` LPE to the shape
4. Change the `Gap X` and/or `Gap Y` distances to nonzero values (choose a value similar to the dimensions of the shape to demonstrate the issue most distinctly)
5. In `File > Document Properties > Display > Display > Display units`, switch to any different unit (I've been using `mm`/`cm`)
6. Observe the unchanged `Gap X` and `Gap Y` distances
7. Perform any of the following:
    - attempt to modify the LPE settings
    - save and reopen the file and select the shape in the reopened file
    - export (to e.g. PDF)

##### Concrete example
Use `mm` for document display units. Create a `50 mm` wide shape with a `Gap X` value of `50 mm`. Change document display units to `cm`.

#### What happened?

The gap distance is not scaled like everything else in the document. The new value displays the same value as was previously selected. The spaces between each of the LPE shape instances still look appropriately sized in the document, but the gap spacing is recalculated on subsequent edit or export, revealing that the layout on the page is dramatically different than was originally intended.

In the concrete example above, the gap remains set to `50 mm`, which is 10x smaller than the shape after changing document display units. Changing the gap to either `500 mm` or `50 cm` restores the original relation.

Issue:
Some control handles aren't antialiased
Issue forked from https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/merge_requests/5624#note_1563473196:

    > I know the answer but we cannot get antialiasing on the rendering right?

## Description

Some on-canvas control handles, for example circular ones, are always rendered without antialiasing. They don't look good!

![image](/uploads/fed4cb2703d05efbe874d9d331fa45b0/image.png)

After https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/merge_requests/5624, the issue remains, albeit changed in appearance:

![image](/uploads/f0d150517281fd25f23efede82ab9f5c/image.png)

## Steps to reproduce

* Open Inkscape.
* Draw a curve.
* Using the node tool, select one of the curve segments.
* Observe the circular control handles.

## Solution

Certain handle types in `canvas-item-ctrl.cpp` still use rendering paths that fill in the pixels manually, without antialiasing. They should all be converted to use Cairo, as is already the case for most handle types.

Path effects become permanent when moved/popped out of path effect group
#### Summary:

When moving a path out of a group that has a path effect, the path effect silently becomes permanently applied, as if object-to-path had been used.

#### Steps to reproduce:

The expected case
- open Inkscape
- create an ellipse
- place that ellipse in a group
- Apply the rotate copies path effect to the group
- using the layers panel, drag the ellipse out of the group
- notice that the object goes back to being a single ellipse, as expected

The unexpected case:

- create a second ellipse
- using object-to-path, turn the ellipse into a path
- place that path in a group
- Apply the rotate copies path effect to the group
- using the layers panel, drag the path out of the group
- notice that the path effect has been permanently applied to the path (as if object-to-path had been used), which is unexpected

This can be reproduced with both the "rotate copies" and "mirror symmetry" path effect (and probably others), so it's likely an issue with group undos and not a particular path effect.

When using objects, you can freely move the objects in and out of a group with the path effect.  When using paths, the path effect becomes automatically applied.

I've also encountered bloating, corruption, and crashes when trying to undo "a "moving a path into a group with a path effect" which could be related.

When moving a path out of a group which has a path effect, I would expect that the path effect would be removed from the path.

The stroke of the box drawn changed from black to red.

Issue:
1.4beta: Node tool handle design obstructs view, makes drawing difficult
#### Summary:

The new node handles design does not help with drawing fine and intricate designs. It is clunky and obstructs the view.

#### Steps to reproduce:
- open Inkscape 1.4beta
- draw something with the Bézier or Pencil tool
- click on a node

#### What happened?

- Node handles are filled, and clunky and obstruct the view, especially adjacent handles that show up when I adjust the selected node's handles are very much in the way of seeing what I'm doing
- When hovering over a node handle or clicking on it, it is barely recognizable that there is a color change (blue - blue)
- Nodes, when selected, no longer have a contrasting color with the fill, nor do they still display the path outline inside them, making it more difficult to achieve and see fine adjustments

#### What should have happened?

- Node handles should be less clunky by default (transparent fill, or at least partially transparent, should be possible)
- Hovering and using a node handle should be clearly visibly separate from it just being there (red! Not blue)
- Selected nodes should still use the inverted color, and the path should be visible through them, not hidden behind
- The color inversion should still be happening where it was happening before

**Old:**

![grafik](/uploads/1b794011e7bb7fbd5303cdff88650220/grafik.png)
![grafik](/uploads/fc02af833b5c18f04ac32083a07bd4e0/grafik.png){width=199 height=200}

_View of path is obstructed by handles. Selected handle is undifferentiable from unselected._


This unfortunately requires the new handles system to support:

* ~~transparency~~ actually, that is implemented. Phew...
* contrasting/inverting colors

which aren't currently implemented in our custom CSS parser, as far as I understand.

#### Summary:
Lists some areas to test just before Inkscape is released to avoid major errors getting into the release.

<details><summary>Previous issues</summary>

Since the 1.0 release we've had to re-release Inkscape multiple times to fix large errors that were not caught. 
For example on Windows:
- 1.0.2 had broken pdf export of text due to a cairo update (https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/issues/2190)
- 1.1.2 (and 1.2alpha? I don't recall) had the same issue as above (https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/issues/3203)
- 1.2   had a dataloss bug in export dialog that usually would go unnoticed until reopen (https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/issues/3600)
     - caused an early 1.2.1 release instead of a repackaging.
- 1.2.1 had a broken Extension Manager due to a new dependency (https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/issues/3695)
- 1.2.2 had crashing on-canvas text due to a missing patch in our internal cairo (which had to be changed last minute due to an upgrade in another package) (https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/issues/3990, prompting this list https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/issues/3990#note_1200107909)
- We also had an issue recently in our ppa with submodules not being updated (since they had to be updated outside of the [inkscape repo](https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/)).
- 1.3.1 had a data-loss bug with shapes that's apparent in browsers (when saving as Plain SVG all shapes get lost) (https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/merge_requests/6090)
</details>

#### Areas to Test

Should be done separately for each platform.

##### Basic tests
1. All dialogs at least open and work (US, German locale)
2. All tools at least work (US, German locale)
3. Text should work! Non-flowed text (create by a click), auto-flowed shape-inside text (create by click-and-drag), auto-flowed fixed width text (created by dragging the bottom-right handle for non-flowed text), text on a path.
4. Importing, embedding, linking images works.
5. Copy/paste works. Check with gradients, text, LPEs, paths within a document, between documents, and to an external application
6. Undo/redo works
7. Raster extensions work, Render extensions work (try 2 of each)
8. Other extensions work (try eps import, a couple render extensions)

##### Export / Interop tests
(can someone add test files here?)
Test the following with more than one moderately complex projects.
1. Save it and reopen it with Inkscape. It should result in the same image.
2. Save as plain SVG and reopen it with Inkscape. Visually it should look identical to the Inkscape SVG.
3. Save as plain SVG and open it with both Chrome and Firefox. Except for missing features (mesh gradients, pages), it should look identical to that in Inkscape.
4. Save as PDF. The PDF shouldn't be corrupted, should look identical with that in Inkscape, and should contain the correct dimensions and metadata.

##### Reactions to bugs we've had before
1. Any new features  (please add them to the release checklist for future releases too)
2. Extension manager can install an extension, clipart import can import a clipart from OpenClipart.
3. Snapping works, doesn't crash
4. Tutorials open and look normal (found via the Help > Tutorials sub-menu)
5. Windows installer, about screen, welcome screen show intended version/image
6. pdf save/export works (with text), including multi-page documents. Check in external pdf reader, and check font list per the pdf's document properties (xreader on Linux, Adobe Reader on Windows both provide this feature). Also try [454.svg](https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inbox/uploads/a5ebf7f4a38f6916be6bff85c99328a7/454.svg)
7. Markers, gradients, patterns, clips, masks, symbols can be applied and remain on saving and reopening the document.
8. Export dialog, save as dialog both work with multiple file formats (try with file of some complexity).
9. @nemanov_oo offered to check clicking to select works on wmii before a new release (https://gitlab.com/inkscape/inkscape/-/issues/2801).
10. Grids, guides, document with checkerboard render properly.

##### This should be in the automated test suite.
1. Command line exports should work
2. Opening a variety of old files
3. Boolean operations work on pairs of items, and groups of items, and text (should be covered by test suite rather than human testing). Note, may not be fully supported yet as of now.

Note also that the automated/unit tests are not lethal on Windows.

# Temporary workaround for broken libgc
if [ -z "$_INKSCAPE_GC" ] ; then

    export _INKSCAPE_GC=disable
fi
```
- run the extracted appimage: `/path/to/squashfs-root/AppRun`

#### What happened?
```
Run experimental bundle that bundles everything
Wrong __data_start/_end pair
Aborted
```

strace: [inkscape-apprun-libgc](/uploads/0d3e6f233288c7516909f89fbaf11c18/inkscape-apprun-libgc)

Note that building an Inkscape appimage in a Ubuntu 20.04 VM, I found that building the `apt source libgc` package with debuild (https://wiki.debian.org/BuildingTutorial) resulted in a crash. However, if I built it using the instructions from https://github.com/ivmai/bdwgc (or cloned that repo, switch to tag: v7.6.4 and built it using the instructions), no crash.

Appimages built off the Ubuntu 18.04 docker image don't have this problem.

Update: I found that when build with debuild, LDFLAGS is set to `-Wl,-Bsymbolic-functions -Wl,-z,relro`. Exporting that flag before `./configure --prefix=/usr` is sufficient to cause the appimage build to crash.

Update(2): Beginning to make more sense, narrowed down to `LDFLAGS="-Wl,-Bsymbolic-functions"`

No crash

Issue:
Native Mac OSX Application for Inkscape
Ultimately, we want signed DMG (non-X) releases of Inkscape 1.0.  This is a top request from many of our users and sponsors.

This means we need to compile Inkscape with Quartz but without X11 and against Gtk3 instead of Gtk2, with current Inkscape master.  Since it will still use Gtk this isn't "Native" in the truest sense of the word, but it will adhere closely to the standard Mac user experience.

This is a master issue for outlining the problem space and linking all bug reports relevant to creation of a native Mac package.  We don't need to link every bug related to Mac, just issues involving the packaging itself, feature development needs, and severely critical bugs.

Breakdown
=========

From what I have gathered, it sounds like we can break this problem up into a few discrete pieces:

(1) Legacy package maintenance
-------------------------------
Legacy packages include the various XQuartz (X11-based) packages currently in use for distributing the 0.92x version of Inkscape.  There have been several different packaging solutions, including through MacPorts and HomeBrew.  Many of our current bug reports and discussions are about these legacy packages; some issues will still be relevant with a native package, some won't.

(2) Dependency versions
-----------------------
Gtk and assorted libs are moving targets, version-wise. Tracking the bleeding edge can be problematic, suggesting using some defined snapshot of them, possibly even shipping them ourselves in the image. This sounds like something that needs more exploration to find the most maintainable solution that gives users the right balance of installation convenience and support.

(3) CMake packaging improvements
--------------------------------
Paths to the share folder, and probably other platform specific stuff could be rolled into the CMake rules, like we've done with Win32. I don't know what the state of this is, but I expect the more we can properly bake into our core CMake scripts, the more maintainable this all will be longer term.

(4) UI/UX glitches and styling issues
-------------------------------------
Things like the behaviors of popup menus and stuff need tweaking. Probably a lot will end up being Gtk upstream troubles, which we'll either need to fix ourselves and send patches upstream, or add workarounds in Inkscape itself. In either case, we need to build a list of upstream bugs to keep track of.

In addition to behavioral problems are also going to be some stylistic oddness - things that work ok functionally but just don't "look" right on a Mac: Spacing of widgets, appearance of custom UI elements, order of things in menus, etc.

(5) Native packaging maintenance efforts
----------------------------------------
If I understand right, Valerioa (and capin maybe?) have worked thorough a lot of the actual problems in getting a native (or native-looking?) build working. Sounds like it needs some productization attention though, to reduce the number of "hacky" steps needed, and maybe get all the fixes integrated properly into the mainline codebases.

(6) Desktop integration
-----------------------
* Preferences handling
* Application and user data files
* Shared resources
* Mapping the XDG spec to the conventions used on Mac OS X
* Default paths
* Copy and Paste
* Native menu integration (e.g. file and print)

(7) External tool integration
-----------------------------
For file format conversion, filters, and extensions we use various 3rd party tools, e.g. Ghostscript, GIMP, etc.  For tools that have good Mac ports we should integrate with them directly, rather than running them on the command line.  For tools that do not have Mac ports, we should look at a) replacing them with equivalent functionalities already present on Mac, b) creating and providing our own packages of these tools, or c) including them in the DMG bundle (which we generally try to avoid to keep file size down).

(8) Testing
-----------
There are going to be several different angles to testing. The packaging correctness and general installation experience need tested. The basic software functionality needs acceptance-level testing. The UI needs UX testing for fit and function with the OS. Bug reports on all discovered issues need filed with good write ups, appropriately tagged, and prioritized.

(9) Maintenance documentation
-----------------------------
A "paint by numbers" style document of the procedure for producing packages when a new Inkscape release is put out, to save future packaging volunteers time and confusion.  These directions will need to be kept up to date and authoritative.

(10) Signing
------------
The end result package needs to be formally signed by us. I'm told there is a $99 cost to get a Developer subscription, which lasts 4-5 years and provides a signing cert that can be used to sign the .app using the `codesign` command.  For listing the app in the MacApp store there is an annual renewal fee.  Some additional research should be done to see if there's any other steps needed.

#### Steps to reproduce

- modify current file, e.g. add a big red circle
- File > Save as template (right above 'import')
- enter a name

- click on save
- close dialog
- close Inkscape
- reopen Inkscape

- red circle on canvas from new default file

### Cause

- the template file is not saved with the correct extension. It is saved as 'default.svg' in the /templates directory, but depending on the language, a language identifier needs to be appended for the program to actually load the file. None is needed for English, that's why it works in English.

void Layout::fitToPathAlign(SVGLength const &startOffset, Path const &path)
{
    double offset = 0.0;

    if (startOffset._set) {
        if (startOffset.unit == SVGLength::PERCENT)
            offset = startOffset.computed * const_cast<Path&>(path).Length();
        else
            offset = startOffset.computed;
    }

    switch (_paragraphs.front().alignment) {
        case CENTER:
            offset -= _getChunkWidth(0) * 0.5;
            break;
        case RIGHT:
            offset -= _getChunkWidth(0);
            break;
        default:
            break;
    }
```

Issue:
Consider pre-compiling python code in distribution packages or during installation
Python tends to save the pre-compiled Python bytecode to .pyc files while executing a script for performance reasons.

This has several implications (at least in our Windows packages):
* Typically Python does not have write access to the installation folder, so if they're not present at install time, it will never create them, which could reduce performance.
* If we ship outdated ones it's even worse, as Python tries to read them each time only to find they're outdated.
* If we don't ship them, but Python creates them at some point (i.e. while running Inkscape with administrative privileges), we have troubles with our uninstallers (see for example inbox#556) as they assume files not previously installed were added by the user and are not safe to delete.

Possible solutions:
* We could ship up-to-date .pyc files - but will they be considered up-to-date on the users system?
* We could create up-to-date .pyc files during installation. This is how Python itself does it. Obviously this requires some effort, would need to be done for each distribution format separately, is fragile (additional code that runs on systems we don't control), and increases install times for users.
* We could ignore the issue and make sure uninstallers delete them / installers warn about them.

Open questions that block a decision (help in investigating those is more than welcome)
* [ ] Are .pyc files useful, i.e. do they actually decrease load times significantly? Do we have numbers?
* [ ] How does Python determine whether a .pyc file is up-to-date? If we create them on one system, do they stay valid on another?
* [ ] Are there safe/established ways to pre-compile to python bytecode (how does Python itself do it for example?) and how hard would it be to add this to our own installers)
